_note_rows_empty_: Same funnel as the A2 draft: an A3 row carries a `consumer` predicate, and gate 3 applies to that predicate exactly as it applies to a gate. 12 candidates -> 0 rows whose consumer the current engine can decide by set comparison alone.

_rejected_rows_.subject: book_reservation
_rejected_rows_.value: If the status is **delayed** or **on time**, the flight has not taken off, cannot be booked.
_rejected_rows_.consumer_that_would_be_required: multi_arg_producer + per-element iteration over a list argument
_rejected_rows_.why: resolve_field calls the producer with exactly one argument; get_flight_status needs two (date, flight_number). The gated value also lives inside args['flights'] (a list of segments), not in a scalar id argument. No set-comparison over a single top-level field can express it.

sources.quote: If the status is **delayed** or **on time**, the flight has not taken off, cannot be booked.
If the status is **flying**, the flight has taken off but not landed, cannot be booked.

_rejected_rows_.subject: update_reservation_flights
_rejected_rows_.value: Basic economy flights cannot be modified.
_rejected_rows_.consumer_that_would_be_required: operation-discriminator (arg-vs-record diff) so a polysemous write tool can carry per-operation preconditions
_rejected_rows_.why: tool-operation polysemy. One write tool performs BOTH 'change flights' (forbidden while cabin is basic economy) and 'change cabin' (explicitly permitted for basic economy by the second quote). A tool-level allow-set on the reservation's cabin therefore FALSE-BLOCKS the permitted operation. Telling the two operations apart requires diffing the `flights` argument against the stored flights = a new checker. Secondary defect: the reservation-level cabin field name is not attested by any allowed source (see _unknown_).

sources.quote: Basic economy flights cannot be modified.
In other cases, all reservations, including basic economy, can change cabin without changing the flights.

_rejected_rows_.subject: update_reservation_flights
_rejected_rows_.value: Cabin cannot be changed if any flight in the reservation has already been flown.
_rejected_rows_.consumer_that_would_be_required: exists_where / all_where over a nested list field
_rejected_rows_.why: existential quantifier over a nested list. resolve_field returns one top-level field; membership in `allow` cannot express 'no element of reservation.flights has status flown'.

sources.quote: Cabin cannot be changed if any flight in the reservation has already been flown.

_rejected_rows_.subject: update_reservation_baggages
_rejected_rows_.value: The user can add but not remove checked bags.
_rejected_rows_.why: order comparison between an argument (total_baggages) and stored state. The engine has membership only; the `constraints` kind ops are {disjoint, equal_len} and both compare two ARGUMENTS, never an argument against a record.

sources.quote: The user can add but not remove checked bags.

_rejected_rows_.subject: (none)
_rejected_rows_.value: The user cannot add insurance after initial booking.
_rejected_rows_.consumer_that_would_be_required: none - the rule is env-mirrored by the absence of the tool
_rejected_rows_.why: No tool to gate. Across the full 14-tool airline inventory, `insurance` appears as an argument of book_reservation ONLY. There is no post-booking insurance tool, so a declaration here would point at nothing and could never fire. This is the airline instance of the banking failure mode (11 of 38 A3 rows aimed at absent tools).

sources.quote: The user cannot add insurance after initial booking.

_rejected_rows_.subject: update_reservation_passengers
_rejected_rows_.value: The user can modify passengers but cannot modify the number of passengers.
_rejected_rows_.why: length equality between an argument list and a stored list. `equal_len` exists but compares two arguments; there is no arg-vs-record form.

sources.quote: The user can modify passengers but cannot modify the number of passengers.
Even a human agent cannot modify the number of passengers.

_rejected_rows_.subject: cancel_reservation
_rejected_rows_.value: If any portion of the flight has already been flown, the agent cannot help and transfer is needed.
_rejected_rows_.consumer_that_would_be_required: exists_where / all_where over a nested list field
_rejected_rows_.why: existential quantifier over a nested list, same shape as C03.

sources.quote: If any portion of the flight has already been flown, the agent cannot help and transfer is needed.

_rejected_rows_.subject: cancel_reservation
_rejected_rows_.value: Otherwise, flight can be cancelled if any of the following is true:
_rejected_rows_.consumer_that_would_be_required: allow_any_of over several resolver paths - and even then one disjunct stays open
_rejected_rows_.why: four-way disjunction. `allow` is a NECESSARY condition (deny when cur not in allow), so encoding any single disjunct false-blocks the other three. The disjunction also mixes a time computation (created_time vs now, 24 hrs) and an OPEN predicate (whether the stated reason is covered by insurance - a judgement, LLM territory per [[52]]/[[22]]).

sources.quote: Otherwise, flight can be cancelled if any of the following is true:
- The booking was made within the last 24 hrs
- The flight is cancelled by airline
- It is a business flight
- The user has travel insurance and the reason for cancellation is covered by insurance.

_rejected_rows_.subject: send_certificate
_rejected_rows_.value: Only compensate if the user is a silver/gold member or has travel insurance or flies business.
_rejected_rows_.consumer_that_would_be_required: allow_any_of across multiple resolver paths (multi-record disjunction)
_rejected_rows_.why: three-way disjunction spanning TWO records (user.membership, reservation.insurance, reservation.cabin) while a check names exactly one resolver_path. `allow:['silver','gold']` on [user_id, get_user_details, membership] is closed and tempting, but it is one disjunct, not the necessary condition: it would deny a regular member who holds travel insurance, whom the policy explicitly permits to be compensated.

sources.quote: Only compensate if the user is a silver/gold member or has travel insurance or flies business.
Do not compensate if the user is regular member and has no travel insurance and flies (basic) economy.

_rejected_rows_.subject: update_reservation_flights
_rejected_rows_.value: Other reservations can be modified without changing the origin, destination, and trip type.
_rejected_rows_.consumer_that_would_be_required: unchanged_fields (arg-derived vs record) - requires a derivation step first
_rejected_rows_.why: argument-vs-record equality on three fields, and worse: update_reservation_flights takes only (cabin, flights, payment_id, reservation_id) - origin, destination and trip type are not call arguments at all, so they would first have to be DERIVED from the flights list. Derivation is not set comparison.

sources.quote: Other reservations can be modified without changing the origin, destination, and trip type.

_rejected_rows_.subject: book_reservation / update_reservation_flights / update_reservation_baggages
_rejected_rows_.value: All payment methods must already be in user profile for safety reasons.
_rejected_rows_.why: member_of: an argument value must belong to a SET resolved from another record. The engine compares a resolved value against a literal allow-list; the direction is reversed and the right-hand side is dynamic. retail's own G7 note already records this exact op as excluded (payment member_of = derived field, [[05]] risk, not included).

sources.quote: All payment methods must already be in user profile for safety reasons.
The payment method must already be in user profile for safety reasons.

_rejected_rows_.subject: update_reservation_flights
_rejected_rows_.value: Cabin class must remain the same across all the flights in the same reservation; changing cabin for just one flight segment is not possible.
_rejected_rows_.consumer_that_would_be_required: none - already enforced by the tool signature
_rejected_rows_.why: vacuous / env-mirrored. update_reservation_flights takes a single scalar `cabin` for the whole call, so no call can express a per-segment cabin. A gate here would never fire. A declaration that cannot fire is worse than none - it inflates A2 volume without changing a single message, which is this strand's whole premise (banking bought a 46x A2 for a 4x delivery).

sources.quote: Cabin class must remain the same across all the flights in the same reservation; changing cabin for just one flight segment is not possible.
